## Declaration and scope

The frozen declaration is
[`count_mixture_lowpass_genome/declaration.R`](count_mixture_lowpass_genome/declaration.R),
with its pre-run
[execution declaration](count_mixture_lowpass_genome/execution_declaration.md).
It commits 200 replicates in each of 90 strata: shares 0/0.02/0.05/0.10/0.20,
same-superpopulation unrelated, other-superpopulation unrelated and IBD1,
at 0.1x, 0.2x and 0.4x, with sequencing error 0.0001 and 0.0002.
Seventy-five strata are primary: 0.1x/0.4x at error 0.0001, and all depths
at error 0.0002. The 15 error-0.0001 strata at 0.2x are secondary.
All 18,000 replicates use site artefact probability 0.002 and fitted excess
homozygosity zero. Statistical criteria and the calibration grid are unchanged;
an incomplete stratum is not evaluated against release targets.

This report is separate from the
[chr20 report](benchmark_count_mixture_lowpass.md); its sections and verdicts
are unchanged. These are phased-genome simulations, not real count-table
calibration-transfer measurements. Correct generating relationships select
which conditional fit is judged; the algorithm does not learn that relationship.

### Frozen release targets

* At shares >= 0.05, absolute mean bias <= 0.005/0.0035/0.0025 at
  0.1/0.2/0.4x. At least 90% of replicates have absolute error <=
  0.025/0.015/0.008 for matched unrelated, 0.020/0.014/0.010 for
  anchored other-population unrelated, or 0.050/0.025/0.015 for matched IBD1.
* Coverage >= 92%, with the exact two-sided 95% binomial interval containing
  the nominal 95% coverage. Null positive claims use `share_lower > 0`;
  their exact one-sided 95% binomial upper bound must be <= 0.075.
* Failed statuses, missing shares and missing/invalid intervals remain in
  denominators. A recovery pass also requires every fit to be `ok_conditional`
  with a finite share and interval. Strata below 200 completions have no verdict.
* Interval width mean/median/90th percentile/maximum and full-range intervals
  are reported. Matched-frequency diagnostics must remain `unresolved`,
  including IBD1; relative scores do not choose a relationship.
* Replicate 1 of each stratum has an independent R moment oracle, exact integer
  counters, and relative moment error <= 1e-10 (absolute near zero). One/four
  DuckDB threads must agree on statuses, missingness and diagnostics; share
  and interval differences must be <= 1e-5, moment differences <= 1e-10.
* No spill. RSS and reported DuckDB peak buffer each have the frozen ceiling
  768 MiB + 3 times (512 bytes per input counts row + live R panels/counts
  + native 256 MiB cap). For the fresh-process scaling series, live R state is
  the largest chromosome panel/count pair. This is a modeled SQL preparation
  allowance, not a measurement of native live state. Native moments are
  bounded independently; joins, validation and ordered preparation dominate
  these SQL workloads. The DuckDB memory setting is 6 GB; measured peak buffer
  is reported separately, not assumed to equal that setting.
* Fixed-block site scaling uses all autosomes at strides 4/2/1 (1x/2x/4x),
  in fresh processes. The end-to-end endpoint timing exponent must be <= 1.25
  if the smallest run takes >= 5 seconds. Query-only timings are also retained.

## Inputs, simulation and provenance

Each autosome's children BCF and matched AF Parquet is resolved and SHA-256
verified through `r/duckhtsbench`. The chr20 AF identity is the ordered rebuild
pinned to `b862fc7d`. Each derived chromosome artifact is registered as
`count_mixture_lowpass_chr<N>_children_haplotypes`; its source identities and
settings are embedded, and the run manifest pins the derived bytes again.
No download is needed. The network-free staging fixture covers allele order,
all four diploid encodings, repeat staging, family-disjoint donors, rejection
of unphased GTs and checksum failure. A full BCF audit checks all children for
unphased GTs, independently of the panel join.

Thirty-six CEU and 56 YRI children remain after selecting one child per family.
Every replicate draws one CEU child as the sample, a distinct CEU child for
same-superpopulation or IBD1, or a YRI child for other-superpopulation.
Different families supply the unrelated genomes; cryptic relatedness is not
independently screened. These are actual phased diploid children, rather than
the chr20 driver's diploids assembled from separate founders. Sample and donor
identity is fixed across all 22 autosomes. IBD1 takes one phased sample
haplotype and one phased donor haplotype, with fixed haplotype labels within
each chromosome and no crossover simulation, matching the chr20 simplification.

The provided `AF_EUR`/`AF_AFR` anchors are used directly, without re-estimation
or clamping. These 1000G AFs include the simulated genomes in their full
2504/3202-genome frequency source: there is no leave-two-out exclusion.
This induces finite-panel dependence between genotypes and frequencies and
can make alignment optimistic relative to held-out transfer. It can alter
baseline heterozygosity, bias and interval calibration; its direction and
size are not isolated here. CEU/YRI are narrower populations than EUR/AFR,
so this campaign does not remove within-superpopulation frequency mismatch.

Depth is Poisson; ALT conditional on depth is binomial with probability
`e + (1 - 2e) * ((1-share)*sample_dosage/2 + share*donor_dosage/2)`.
With probability 0.002 a site's ALT count is uniform on 0..depth. Every site's
depth and the same random draws are retained. Only covered sites enter the
bulk-loaded counts table; full-panel sites, zero-depth sites, excluded sites
and unavailable sites are reported separately per replicate. Macro-native QC
therefore describes covered input rows, not all simulated sites. The macro uses
`block_bases := 10000000`, `min_blocks := 30`, default
maximum depth 8, and the same error/artefact calibration used to generate counts.
The native extension and every `src/` file are unchanged.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE)
result_dir <- "count_mixture_lowpass_genome/results"
read_result <- function(name) {
  path <- file.path(result_dir, name)
  if (endsWith(name, ".rds.gz")) readRDS(path) else read.csv(path)
}
metadata <- jsonlite::fromJSON(file.path(result_dir, "metadata.json"), simplifyVector = FALSE)
strata <- read_result("strata.csv")
fits <- read_result("replicates.rds.gz")
performance <- read_result("performance.rds.gz")
checks <- read_result("oracle_and_threads.csv")
scaling <- read_result("scaling.csv")
phase <- read_result("phase.csv")
campaign_timing <- read_result("campaign_timing.csv")
primary <- strata[strata$primary, ]
stopifnot(nrow(strata) == 90L, all(strata$replicates == 200L),
          nrow(performance) == 18000L, nrow(fits) == 30000L, nrow(checks) == 90L)
show_table <- function(x, digits = 4) knitr::kable(x, digits = digits)
```

```{r provenance, results='asis'}
cat("Declaration commit: `", metadata$declaration_commit, "`; batching amendment: `",
    metadata$batching_amendment_commit, "`; execution amendment: `",
    metadata$execution_amendment_commit, "`. Campaign driver revision: `",
    metadata$sources$revision, "`.\n\n", sep = "")
cat(metadata$sources$runtime$R, "; DuckDB R ", metadata$sources$runtime$duckdb, ".\n\n", sep = "")
cat("Input/extension/driver hashes: [metadata.json](count_mixture_lowpass_genome/results/metadata.json).\n\n")

    " MiB; the limit is 4 GiB. All full-depth inputs contain ", unique(performance$sites), " panel sites.\n", sep = "")
```

### Execution

Run from the worktree root with RBCFTools' bundled bcftools in the private R
library, not a PATH executable. Staging and identity verification are outside
timed simulations. Recovery uses fourteen long-lived R/DuckDB workers,
`nice -n 10`, on CPU IDs **0–5,12–19**, with one DuckDB thread per worker;
explicit identity probes also use four threads. Each worker loads chromosome
panels once. Microbatches contain 4/2/1 replicates at depths 0.1/0.2/0.4,
with one macro call grouping by sample identity. BLAS/OpenMP are limited to
one thread. Input identities and all-child phase are verified once at startup.
Per-seed outputs are atomically written under the manifest SHA-256, and resumed
only when source/input identities and settings match.

```sh
taskset -c 0-5,12-19 env R_LIBS=/tmp/RBCFTools-release-lib \
  Rscript benchmarks/count_mixture_lowpass_genome/stage.R 1 build/release/duckhts.duckdb_extension
# Repeat staging for chromosomes 2–22.
taskset -c 0-5,12-19 nice -n 10 env R_LIBS=/tmp/RBCFTools-release-lib \
  Rscript benchmarks/count_mixture_lowpass_genome/run.R build/release/duckhts.duckdb_extension /tmp/lowpass-genome
```

Full per-replicate native outputs and process logs are retained by the runner;
checked-in gzip RDS tables preserve every seed, conditional share/interval/status,
family-disjoint identity and performance denominator, with lossless doubles and
categorical text labels. Read them with `readRDS()`. Missing results are not
replaced by successful draws. Native outputs can be reconstructed from the
registered artifacts, manifest, declaration and seeds.

### Covered-site and microbatch checks

```{r covered_checks}
equivalence <- read_result("covered_equivalence.csv")
probe <- read_result("microbatch_probe.csv")
control_fits <- read_result("covered_control_fits.rds.gz")
strict_exact <- vapply(control_fits$controls, function(x) {
  identical(x$full[control_fits$fields], x$covered[control_fits$fields],
            num.eq = FALSE, single.NA = FALSE)
}, logical(1L))
stopifnot(length(strict_exact) == 9L, all(strict_exact))
show_table(equivalence[c("depth", "replicate", "seed", "exact", "sites", "zero_depth_sites",
                        "excluded_sites", "unavailable_sites")])
show_table(probe)
```

All-site and covered-site shares, interval endpoints, standard errors,
singles shares, pair residuals, statuses, diagnostics, blocks and pair blocks
must be bit-identical in all nine controls before using the shortcut. Covered
count rows and QC also match the original simulator exactly. The declaration
retains the full-site controls' peak-buffer caveat; campaign batches are chosen
from the covered-input measurements, not from the configured memory setting.
The native control tables are retained for direct IEEE-bit comparison.

## Release outcomes

```{r gates}
interior <- primary[primary$truth >= .05, ]
null <- primary[primary$truth == 0, ]
show_table(data.frame(
  criterion = c("Interior bias", "90% absolute error", "Coverage and binomial compatibility",
                "Null false-positive upper bound", "Matched diagnostic", "All release criteria"),
  evaluated_strata = c(nrow(interior), nrow(interior), nrow(primary), nrow(null),
                       sum(primary$relationship != "other"), nrow(primary)),
  passing_strata = c(sum(interior$bias_pass, na.rm = TRUE), sum(interior$accuracy_pass, na.rm = TRUE),
                    sum(primary$coverage_pass, na.rm = TRUE), sum(null$null_pass, na.rm = TRUE),
                    sum(primary$diagnostic_pass[primary$relationship != "other"]),
                    sum(primary$release_pass, na.rm = TRUE))))
```

### Detection and recovery

Positive-call rates below mean `share_lower > 0` under the supplied generating
relationship. They are observations, not a separate release gate or relationship
classification. Null positive calls are subject to the declared binomial gate.

```{r primary_results}
show_table(primary[c("relationship", "depth", "error", "truth", "replicates", "mean_share", "bias",
                     "absolute_error_90", "accuracy", "coverage", "detection", "release_pass")])
```

```{r nulls}
show_table(primary[primary$truth == 0, c("relationship", "depth", "error", "replicates", "mean_share",
                                      "detection", "null_upper", "null_pass")])
```

### Intervals, statuses and ambiguous relationships

```{r intervals}
show_table(primary[c("relationship", "depth", "error", "truth", "interval_mean", "interval_median",
                     "interval_90", "interval_max", "full_range_intervals", "missing_interval")])
```

```{r statuses}
status <- read_result("statuses.csv")
show_table(aggregate(count ~ relationship_model + status + relation_diagnostic, status, sum))
show_table(data.frame(failed_statuses = sum(strata$failed_status),
                     missing_shares = sum(strata$missing_share),
                     missing_intervals = sum(strata$missing_interval),
                     failed_jackknife_refits = sum(fits$jackknife_failed_refits)))
```

Both matched conditional models remain in the gzip table. Their existence and
numerically successful statuses do not resolve the same-superpopulation
relationship or establish calibrated confidence intervals. Across all matched
native rows, 21,684 diagnostics are `unresolved` and 2,316 are `uninformative`;
the strict all-replicates-`unresolved` criterion passes in 31/50 primary matched
strata. The criterion is not broadened to include `uninformative`.

show_table(strata[!strata$primary, c("relationship", "depth", "error", "truth", "replicates", "mean_share",

## Independent numerical checks

```{r oracle}
show_table(data.frame(checked_strata = nrow(checks),
  max_R_moment_error = max(checks$moment_error), counter_failures = sum(!checks$counters_exact),
  status_failures = sum(!checks$status_equal), share_missingness_failures = sum(!checks$share_missing_equal),
  interval_missingness_failures = sum(!checks$interval_missing_equal),
  diagnostic_failures = sum(!checks$diagnostic_equal),
  max_thread_share_error = max(checks$share_error), max_thread_interval_error = max(checks$interval_error),
  max_thread_moment_error = max(checks$thread_moment_error),
  solo_batch_failures = sum(!checks$batch_exact),
  bit_identical_thread_checks = sum(checks$bit_identical)), digits = 14)
```

The R oracle reconstructs all moments and covered-input QC counters for every
physical chromosome/10 Mb block, using direct weighted cross-products, not the
SQL expressions. Full-panel and zero-depth QC are retained separately for every
seed; zero-depth rows contribute no moments. The SQL probe exposes the actual
moment rows passed to the native aggregate. No implementation output is used as its own oracle.

## Performance and scaling

```{r campaign_timing}
show_table(campaign_timing)
cat("Simulated site exposures: ", format(sum(performance$sites), scientific = FALSE),
    "; covered counts rows: ", format(sum(performance$covered_sites), scientific = FALSE),
    "; output rows: ", nrow(fits), ".\n", sep = "")
```

The 200-replicate pilot took 243.3 seconds (1.216 seconds per replicate).
The concurrent campaign took 10,373.5 seconds (2.88 hours); the whole command,
including startup identity/phase audits and the pilot, took 3:08:37.
The original eight-hour budget is met, but the roughly 1.5-hour target is missed.
The assigned fourteen logical CPUs comprise three SMT core pairs and eight
other cores on an Intel i5-13500; a single-worker probe did not predict
concurrent throughput. No strata or replicates are dropped to meet the target.

Campaign timings are amortized within each microbatch and include neither
per-replicate process startup nor repeated panel reading. Worker RSS is a
long-lived-process high-water mark, not an isolated per-replicate measurement.

```{r campaign_performance}
show_table(aggregate(cbind(simulation_seconds, loading_seconds, fit_seconds, wall_seconds) ~ stratum,
                     performance, mean))
show_table(aggregate(cbind(sites, covered_sites, zero_depth_sites, excluded_sites,
                          unavailable_sites) ~ stratum, performance, mean))
```

Fresh isolated process timings below include process startup, extension load,
artifact reading, count simulation, ingestion and fitting in the wall total.
The simulation column covers chromosome reading/simulation/ingestion; fit time
covers only the macro query. Peak RSS covers the entire process. These runs
exclude the R oracle and thread probes. Scaling retains all autosomes and
physical blocks while using strides 4/2/1, repeated three times at each depth.
Input artifacts are warm cached. No disk spill is allowed.

```{r scaling}
show_table(scaling[c("depth", "stride", "repetition", "sites", "output_rows", "wall_seconds",
                     "simulation_seconds", "fit_seconds", "rss_bytes", "peak_buffer_bytes", "spill_bytes")])
for (depth in unique(scaling$depth)) {
  x <- scaling[scaling$depth == depth, ]
  med <- aggregate(wall_seconds ~ sites, x, median)
  exponent <- log(tail(med$wall_seconds, 1) / med$wall_seconds[[1L]]) /
    log(tail(med$sites, 1) / med$sites[[1L]])
  cat("\nDepth ", depth, ": endpoint exponent ", round(exponent, 4),
      if (med$wall_seconds[[1L]] >= 5) paste0("; gate ", if (exponent <= 1.25) "met" else "FAIL")
      else "; timing gate not evaluated (smallest run < 5 seconds)", ".\n", sep = "")
}
```

```{r memory}
show_table(data.frame(
  workload = c("Campaign/probes", "Isolated scaling"),
  observations = c(nrow(performance), nrow(scaling)),
  max_RSS_GiB = c(max(performance$rss_bytes), max(scaling$rss_bytes)) / 1024^3,
  max_buffer_GiB = c(max(performance$peak_buffer_bytes), max(scaling$peak_buffer_bytes)) / 1024^3,
  max_spill_bytes = c(max(performance$spill_bytes, checks$spill_bytes), max(scaling$spill_bytes)),
  RSS_ceiling_failures = c(sum(performance$rss_bytes > performance$memory_ceiling_bytes),
                           sum(scaling$rss_bytes > scaling$memory_ceiling_bytes)),
  buffer_ceiling_failures = c(sum(performance$peak_buffer_bytes > performance$memory_ceiling_bytes),
                              sum(scaling$peak_buffer_bytes > scaling$memory_ceiling_bytes))))
```

The nearest checked-in baseline is the chr20 report's fixed-site/fixed-group
scaling experiment. It has different site counts, blocks, population-frequency
construction and workload; these results do not establish a performance
regression or absence of one. The production SQL/native path is unchanged.

## Interpretation

Only 30/75 primary strata meet every declared release criterion. At a 5% share,
0.1x gives positive interval lower limits in 199–200/200 unrelated replicates
and 160–165/200 IBD1 replicates; at 0.4x all tested relationships give 200/200.
Those call rates are not a calibrated detection limit. Five of fifteen primary
null strata fail the false-positive upper-bound criterion, and no primary null
stratum meets every criterion. Bias passes in 40/45 interior strata, point
accuracy in 37/45, and coverage in 53/75 primary strata. Ten generating-model
fits lack intervals; no missing intervals or failed statuses are filtered.

Release criteria are assessed only for completed 200-replicate strata, under
the provided frequency anchors and generating relationship. Detection, point
recovery and calibrated coverage are distinct outcomes. An `ok_conditional`
status is a numerical fit status, not a release-validation verdict. In-panel
frequencies, linked finite genomes, within-superpopulation mismatch and fixed
IBD1 haplotypes limit transfer to independent low-pass datasets. Real-count
genome-wide calibration transfer is not evaluated.
